pois.name: Teatro Nacional de São Carlos
pois.blurb: The Teatro Nacional de São Carlos is an opera house in Lisbon, Portugal. It was inaugurated in 1793 and remains the country’s principal historic venue for opera performances.

themeConnection.text: São Carlos opened in 1793 and continues as Lisbon’s permanent public opera house with regular opera and musical performances.

pois.name: Odesa National Academic Opera and Ballet Theatre
pois.wikipediaTitle: Odesa National Academic Theater of Opera and Ballet
pois.blurb: The Odesa National Academic Theater of Opera and Ballet is the oldest theatre in Odesa, Ukraine. Its present building opened in 1887 and remains an active venue for opera and ballet.

themeConnection.text: The Odesa Opera occupies the theatre site established in the nineteenth century, with the current building opened in 1887 and an ongoing opera and ballet programme.

pois.name: Estates Theatre
pois.blurb: The Estates Theatre (in Czech: Stavovské divadlo) is a historic theatre in Prague, Czech Republic.

themeConnection.text: Estates Theatre is a historic Prague theatre opened in 1783 that remains a functioning public venue within the National Theatre’s regular programme.

pois.name: Teatro di San Carlo
pois.blurb: The Real Teatro di San Carlo ("Royal Theatre of Saint Charles"), as originally named by the Bourbon monarchy but today known simply as the Teatro (di) San Carlo, is a historic opera house in Naples, Italy, connected to the Royal Palace and adjacent to the Piazza del Plebiscito.

themeConnection.text: Teatro di San Carlo opened in 1737 and continues to operate as a permanent Naples opera house with regular public performances.

pois.name: Teatro Argentina
pois.blurb: The Teatro Argentina is an opera house and theatre in Rome, Italy. It was inaugurated in 1732 and continues to function as one of the city’s principal venues for live performance.

themeConnection.text: Teatro Argentina is a Roman theatre opened in 1732 and remains a functioning public venue presenting scheduled drama, opera, and other live theatre.

pois.name: Teatro Amazonas
pois.blurb: The Amazon Theatre (Portuguese: Teatro Amazonas) is an opera house located in Manaus, Brazil, in the heart of the Amazon rainforest.

themeConnection.text: Teatro Amazonas opened in 1896 and remains a fixed Manaus opera and theatre venue that presents publicly scheduled performances.

pois.name: Royal Opera House
pois.blurb: The Royal Opera House (ROH) is a theatre in Covent Garden, central London. The building is often referred to as simply Covent Garden, after a previous use of the site.

themeConnection.text: The Royal Opera House occupies the Covent Garden site of earlier theatre buildings dating to the eighteenth century and remains a regularly operating venue for opera and ballet.

pois.name: Teatro Español
pois.blurb: The Teatro Español is a public theatre in Madrid, Spain. The site has been used for theatrical performances since the sixteenth century, and the current theatre presents regular dramatic productions.

themeConnection.text: Teatro Español is Madrid’s historic municipal theatre, tracing public performances at the site to 1583 and continuing as a regular drama venue.

pois.name: Manoel Theatre
pois.blurb: Teatru Manoel (Maltese for "Manoel Theatre"; Italian: Teatro Manoel) is a theatre and important performing arts venue in Malta.

themeConnection.text: The Manoel Theatre opened in 1732 and remains a permanent Valletta performance venue with public programmes of theatre, opera, and music.

pois.name: Teatro Massimo
pois.blurb: The Teatro Massimo is an opera house and performing arts venue in Palermo, Sicily. It was opened in 1897 and is Italy’s largest theatre building, still presenting performances.

themeConnection.text: Teatro Massimo opened in 1897 and remains Palermo’s permanent opera and performance venue, with publicly scheduled productions.

pois.name: Vienna State Opera
pois.blurb: The Vienna State Opera is an opera house and opera company based in Vienna, Austria. The building opened as the Vienna Court Opera in 1869 and presents a large annual programme.

themeConnection.text: The Vienna State Opera opened in 1869 as the Court Opera and remains a permanent opera and ballet house with a regular public season.

pois.name: Bolshoi Theatre
pois.blurb: The Bolshoi Theatre is a historic theatre in Moscow, Russia, designed for opera and ballet performances. The present building opened in 1856 after earlier Bolshoi theatres occupied the site.

themeConnection.text: The Bolshoi Theatre is a continuously recognized Moscow opera and ballet institution whose present building opened in 1856 and remains publicly programmed.

pois.name: Teatro Nacional Sucre
pois.blurb: The Teatro Nacional Sucre is a theatre in Quito, Ecuador, named for Antonio José de Sucre. It opened in 1886 and is an active venue for theatre, opera, dance, and music.

themeConnection.text: Teatro Nacional Sucre opened in 1886 and, following restoration at the same site, operates as Quito’s permanent public theatre.

pois.name: Teatro de Cristóbal Colón
pois.blurb: The Teatro de Cristóbal Colón is Colombia’s national theatre, located in Bogotá. It was inaugurated in 1892 and continues to present theatre, opera, ballet, and other live performances.

themeConnection.text: Bogotá’s Teatro de Cristóbal Colón opened in 1892 and remains a permanent public theatre for opera, ballet, concerts, and dramatic performance.

pois.name: Hungarian State Opera
pois.blurb: The Hungarian State Opera House is a neo-Renaissance opera house located in central Budapest. It opened in 1884 and remains an important venue for opera and ballet performances.

themeConnection.text: The Hungarian State Opera House opened in 1884 and remains Budapest’s principal permanent venue for scheduled opera and ballet performances.

pois.name: Teatro alla Scala
pois.blurb: La Scala is an opera house in Milan, Italy. The theatre was inaugurated in 1778 and has remained a major venue for opera and ballet, with regular scheduled seasons.

themeConnection.text: La Scala opened in 1778 on the site of the Teatro Ducale and remains one of Milan’s permanent public opera and ballet venues.

pois.name: Mariinsky Theatre
pois.blurb: The Mariinsky Theatre is a historic theatre of opera and ballet in Saint Petersburg, Russia. It opened in 1860 and continues to present performances by its opera and ballet companies.

themeConnection.text: The Mariinsky Theatre’s historic main building opened in 1860 and remains a permanent public venue for opera and ballet in Saint Petersburg.

pois.name: Gran Teatre del Liceu
pois.blurb: The Gran Teatre del Liceu is an opera house on La Rambla in Barcelona. It opened in 1847, was rebuilt after fires, and continues to present regular opera and ballet performances.

themeConnection.text: The Liceu opened in 1847 and, despite rebuilding after fires, remains an operating Barcelona opera house at the established La Rambla site.

pois.name: Teatro Comunale di Bologna
pois.blurb: The Teatro Comunale di Bologna is an opera house in Bologna, Italy. Its first performance took place in 1763, and the theatre remains active with regular opera and concert seasons.

themeConnection.text: Teatro Comunale di Bologna opened in 1763 and continues to operate as a public opera venue at its historic city-centre site.

pois.name: Palais Garnier
pois.blurb: The Palais Garnier is a historic opera house in Paris, France. It was built from 1861 to 1875 for the Paris Opera and continues to host opera, ballet, and other performances.

themeConnection.text: The Palais Garnier is a permanent opera and ballet venue opened in 1875 and remains part of the Paris Opera’s publicly programmed performance network.

clue.text: A regularly operating opera-and-ballet house occupies a Covent Garden site whose earlier theatres were destroyed by fires; its surviving 1858 façade and horseshoe auditorium were extensively reconstructed in the 1990s.

theme.title: Operating Pre-1900 Theatres in Cities
theme.introduction: Across old city streets, stage doors still open onto velvet, brass, and living echoes of centuries of performance.
theme.inclusionCriteria: Include a location only when every condition is met: (1) it is an individually named theatre, opera house, playhouse, or equivalent venue whose principal function is presenting live theatrical, operatic, ballet, or musical performances; (2) the named venue or its continuously recognized predecessor began public performance at the same identifiable site on or before 31 December 1899; (3) the venue currently operates as a permanent performance venue and has regularly scheduled public performances on the date of play; (4) the venue occupies a fixed, mappable building or complex with a public entrance that can be treated as one exact location; (5) it lies within the current administrative boundary of a present-day city or incorporated urban municipality; and (6) ordinary members of the public can attend performances, whether ticketed or free. Rebuilt venues qualify when the theatre institution or venue remains at the same identifiable site. The theme has at least 35 plausible locations, including: Royal Opera House (London); Theatre Royal Drury Lane (London); Theatre Royal Haymarket (London); Bristol Old Vic (Bristol); Palais Garnier (Paris); Comédie-Française, Salle Richelieu (Paris); Théâtre du Châtelet (Paris); Vienna State Opera (Vienna); Hungarian State Opera (Budapest); Estates Theatre (Prague); National Theatre (Prague); Bolshoi Theatre (Moscow); Mariinsky Theatre (Saint Petersburg); Odesa National Academic Opera and Ballet Theatre (Odesa); Teatro alla Scala (Milan); Teatro di San Carlo (Naples); Teatro Argentina (Rome); Teatro Massimo (Palermo); Teatro Olimpico (Vicenza); Teatro Comunale di Bologna (Bologna); Teatro Español (Madrid); Teatro de la Zarzuela (Madrid); Teatro Real (Madrid); Gran Teatre del Liceu (Barcelona); Teatro Nacional de São Carlos (Lisbon); Teatro Nacional D. Maria II (Lisbon); Manoel Theatre (Valletta); Teatro Amazonas (Manaus); Teatro Nacional Sucre (Quito); Teatro de Cristóbal Colón (Bogotá); Teatro Municipal de Santiago (Santiago); Teatro Solís (Montevideo); Teatro Degollado (Guadalajara); Teatro Morelos (Aguascalientes); Teatro de la Paz (San Luis Potosí); Teatro Calderón (Valladolid); Teatro Arriaga (Bilbao); Teatro Romea (Murcia); Teatro Principal (Zaragoza); Teatro Municipal de Valparaíso (Valparaíso); Tbilisi Opera and Ballet Theatre (Tbilisi); Teatro de la República (Querétaro); Grand Theatre of Warsaw (Warsaw); Teatro Regio (Turin).
